auth.description: Front API token sent as a bearer
auth.name: front.api_token
auth.subject: unstated

config.help: In Front, open Settings → API & Integrations → API, and create a new token. A token is scoped to the teammate who creates it and to the scopes granted when it is created — replying and tagging require write scopes, not just read ones
config.label: API token
config.name: api_token

description: Front shared inbox: read and reply to conversations, and tag them

operations.description: List one conversation, confirming the token resolves and carries at least read access. Takes no parameters other than the page bound

params.description: Records to fetch; one is enough to prove the credential works
params.name: limit

_results.description: Up to `limit` conversations. Empty is still a successful credential check — a company can genuinely have none yet

operations.description: List the company's conversations in reverse chronological order (most recently updated first), first page only — this connector cannot follow Front's next-page link (see providers/front.toml's header comment). Front's structured search filter (`q`) is not accepted here: it is a bracket-notation object this pipeline cannot encode as a query string

params.description: Max conversations to return in this one page, up to Front's own cap of 100. Does not change how many pages exist, only how large this one is
params.name: limit

_pagination.description: Carries `next`, a full absolute URL to the following page when more conversations exist. This connector cannot follow it — Front's cursor is an opaque, server-issued token unconstructable by a caller, and unencodable here regardless (C-30) — so a non-null `next` means more conversations exist beyond this first page only

next.description: Unusable here; see this field's own description

_results.description: This page's conversations, each `{id, subject, status, assignee, recipient, tags, created_at, ...}`

status.description: Front's own conversation status, e.g. `assigned`, `unassigned`, `archived` or `deleted`

operations.description: Get one conversation's metadata: subject, status, assignee, recipient and tags. Does not return its messages — use front-conversation-message-list for those

params.description: The conversation's id, an opaque string prefixed `cnv_` (e.g. `cnv_55c8c149`) that a model must not invent — discover it from front-conversation-list or front-verify
params.name: conversation_id

assignee.description: The assigned teammate, `{id, email, first_name, last_name}` — absent (`null`) when unassigned

recipient.description: The conversation's primary counterparty, `{name, handle, role}` — `handle` is an email address or phone number depending on the originating channel

operations.description: List the messages in a conversation in reverse chronological order (newest first), first page only — this connector cannot follow Front's next-page link (see providers/front.toml's header comment). Each message's `body`/`text` is the actual correspondence exchanged on this conversation

params.description: The conversation's id, an opaque string prefixed `cnv_` (e.g. `cnv_55c8c149`) that a model must not invent — discover it from front-conversation-list or front-verify
params.name: conversation_id

params.description: Max messages to return in this one page, up to Front's own cap of 100
params.name: limit

_pagination.description: Carries `next`, a full absolute URL to the following page. This connector cannot follow it — see front-conversation-list's own response_schema for why — so a non-null `next` means more messages exist beyond this first page only

next.description: Unusable here; see this field's own description

_results.description: This page's messages, each `{id, type, is_inbound, author, recipients, subject, body, text, created_at}`

author.description: The teammate who sent this message — absent (`null`) on an inbound message, since nobody on the team authored it

body.description: The message content, HTML for most channels

is_inbound.description: True for a message received from the outside party, false for one sent from Front

recipients.description: Each `{name, handle, role}`; `role` is one of `from`, `to`, `cc`, `bcc` or `reply-to`

type.description: The channel kind this message travelled over, e.g. `email`, `sms` or `intercom`

operations.description: Reply to a conversation, using its own existing recipients, channel and sender identity — this connector cannot override any of those (see providers/front.toml's header comment). Front queues delivery: the response is an acknowledgement, not the sent message, and is not visible to the recipient until Front actually delivers it

params.description: The conversation's id, an opaque string prefixed `cnv_` (e.g. `cnv_55c8c149`) that a model must not invent — discover it from front-conversation-list or front-verify
params.name: conversation_id

params.description: The reply's content. Sent as-is to the conversation's existing recipients over its existing channel — this operation cannot redirect it to a different recipient list, channel or sender (C-56; see providers/front.toml's header comment)
params.name: body

response_schema.description: An acknowledgement that Front accepted the reply for delivery, not the sent message itself

message_uid.description: A resource alias for the queued message. Not a `msg_`-prefixed id and not usable as one — Front assigns the real id only once delivery completes

operations.description: Apply one or more existing tags to a conversation. Applying a tag the conversation already carries changes nothing — Front does not duplicate it. Answers 204 with an empty body on success

params.description: The conversation's id, an opaque string prefixed `cnv_` (e.g. `cnv_55c8c149`) that a model must not invent — discover it from front-conversation-list or front-verify
params.name: conversation_id

params.description: The existing tag ids to apply, each an opaque string prefixed `tag_` that a model must not invent — discover them from a conversation's own `tags` field (front-conversation-get) or from Front's tag settings
params.name: tag_ids
